text:
Alex Kim: Heads up — main is red after the pre-commit rev bump in infra-hooks. Failing on a mix of mypy + rustfmt. CI job: tools/precommit-checks.
CI Bot: build failed — pre-commit hooks failed (exit 1). See job: https://ci.internal/redwood/4521
Priya Nair: I saw this earlier, looks like the pre-commit order change caused rustfmt to reformat before pyright stubs get generated.
Sam Rodriguez: Can you paste the failing output?
Alex Kim: sure, here's the tail:
```
+ mypy repo/
repo/service/handlers.py:214: error: Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type "None", variable has type "str")
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 123 source files)

+ rustfmt --check
Diff in src/kvcache/mod.rs at line 42:
-    let mut buf = Vec::new();
+    let mut buffer = Vec::new();
``` 
Jules: hmm, that's two unrelated failures — mypy complaining about a new optional and rustfmt complaining about renamed var (we didn't rename that). Could be generated code not up to date.
Maya Patel: I suspect the pre-commit hook that runs stubgen -> pyright changed order with format -> rustfmt. If stubgen runs after format, the python type stubs may not exist for some modules during typecheck.
Priya Nair: Agreed. Quick repro: run `tools/ci local-precommit --order=latest` on master; I can run a bisect if someone points at suspected commit range.
Alex Kim: The pre-commit bump PR merged in the infra team 5 commits ago. Can we bisect commits 5..HEAD? I'm short on cycles.
Sam Rodriguez: I can do a bisect, but need a command to run in CI to speed up. Suggestion: `git bisect start --good HEAD~6 --bad HEAD && ./tools/ci bisect-precommit` — our bisect helper parallelizes checks.
Priya Nair: run that on your machine and ping me, I'll watch. If it's flaky, we should pin to previous hook rev as a temporary revert.
CI Bot: triage note — rerun requested by @Sam Rodriguez for build 4521. Command: /rerun job tools/precommit-checks
Jules: Can we also check for flaky test noise? There's a failing test in rust kvcache that looks intermittent: `kvcache::tests::eviction_on_overflow` has failed once in 12 runs.
Maya Patel: That test has a race when run with parallel format step; formatting touched code that affects test ordering in harness. Weird but plausible.
Alex Kim: Plan: Sam bisects to find the offending pre-commit rev. If found, either pin back or add ordering fix to the pre-commit meta. Meanwhile I'll /rerun the CI job to see if it's transient.
Sam Rodriguez: starting bisect now, ETA ~20m. Will post results.
triage-bot: noted — assigning incident ENG-5235 to Alex Kim and Sam Rodriguez. :eyes:
Sam Rodriguez: bisect found culprit: commit c3d9f2a — pre-commit: reorder hooks so rustfmt runs earlier. Reverting that ordering locally makes CI green.
Priya Nair: nice catch. Proposal: open PR to revert ordering, include a test in tools/ci that validates stubgen run before typechecking in python jobs.
Alex Kim: I'll open the revert PR and add the CI check. Sam — can you trigger the /rerun and then merge if green?
Sam Rodriguez: rerun kicked, job passed this time (flaky run). But since bisect found a deterministic break with the ordering revert makes it green, I'm going to land the revert after CI passes twice.
Jules: capturing postmortem notes: avoid changing hook ordering without a cross-language smoke run. Add to infra checklist.
CI Bot: build 4521 rerun passed. Reaction :party_parrot: from @Maya Patel.
Maya Patel: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a small infra PR to pin ordering and add a smoke test in `tools/ci`.
Alex Kim: awesome — closing the loop here. If anyone sees more red after revert/merge, ping this thread.
